title: New Postal Products
summary:
This Federal Register page highlights three things: upcoming closed review meetings for arts grants, a new round of postal shipping contracts under review, and disaster loan aid for Illinois businesses hit by water contamination.

The National Endowment for the Arts will hold closed panel meetings in late January 2026 to review applications in dance, arts education, and folk and traditional arts. That’s a routine part of how grants get decided. Applicants, cultural organizations, educators, and tradition bearers could benefit as funding decisions move forward. Those seeking more transparency might be disappointed that these reviews are not open to the public, though confidentiality is intended to protect sensitive applicant information.

The Postal Regulatory Commission is reviewing new agreements the United States Postal Service filed with large shippers, including changes to an international contract and several new domestic shipping contracts across Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, and Ground Advantage services. The public can comment on certain filings by November 17, 2025, while some standardized contracts move through a faster review without public comment. High‑volume shippers may gain tailored rates and service options, and the Postal Service could strengthen its competitive position. Smaller businesses that don’t qualify for negotiated deals might worry about a widening gap in pricing power, and competitors could see increased pressure. For everyday customers, effects are uncertain; downstream changes could influence pricing and service, but details are not public.

The Small Business Administration declared an economic injury disaster for Coles County, Illinois, and neighboring counties due to algal bloom water contamination last summer. Impacted small businesses and nonprofits can apply for working‑capital loans through August 6, 2026. This offers a financial lifeline to keep operations going despite lost revenue. Organizations outside the declared area or those already facing heavy debt loads may find access or repayment challenging, and loans are not a replacement for lost income.

Overall, these notices show government machinery at work: arts grants advancing, shipping markets adjusting through negotiated deals, and disaster relief opening for affected communities. The benefits and trade‑offs will vary by who you are—an artist or educator, a shipper big or small, or a local business recovering from a tough season.
